notes.claim: Given two points on a line, find the slope between them, then solve for the y-intercept in y = mx + b.
The equation of a line can be found from its gradient and one point on it.
The gradient comes first, found by dividing the difference in y by the difference in x.

sources.title: Module 3 (M3) - Algebra - Coordinates and graphs - BBC Bitesize
sources.quote: To find the gradient of a line joining two points, divide the difference in the y-coordinates by the difference in the x-coordinates

sources.title: Slope-intercept equation from two points - Khan Academy
sources.quote: Given two points on a line, we can write an equation for that line by finding the slope between those points, then solving for the y-intercept in the slope-intercept equation y=mx+b.

sources.title: Equation of a straight line - Determining the equation of a straight line - National 5 Maths Revision - BBC Bitesize
sources.quote: We can find the equation of a straight line when given the gradient and a point on the line
